title: Broomfield
name: Broomfield
metaDescription: Broomfield 1031 exchange coordination for corporate office near Interlocken and retail near Flatiron Marketplace, with attention to boot exposure at high price points.

sections.html: Broomfield is its own city and its own county, a rare combination in Colorado, and that split identity shows up in how deals get done here. Corporate campuses along US-36 carry the office side of the market, and Flatiron Marketplace carries the retail side. A buyer used to dealing with a county government layered on top of a separate city government elsewhere in the metro will find that step simplified here, since one government handles both.

sections.heading: A Corporate Corridor With Retail Attached
sections.html: Interlocken and the broader US-36 corridor have drawn corporate and tech tenants for years, which means Broomfield office product tends to trade differently than office in Denver proper, longer leases, larger single-tenant buildings, less speculative churn. Flatiron Marketplace and the surrounding retail nodes serve both the local workforce and drive-through traffic between Denver and Boulder. That dual role, corporate campus and commuter waypoint, gives Broomfield a broader base of demand than a typical single-industry suburb.

sections.heading: What's Actually Available to Trade
sections.html:
Single-tenant and multi-tenant office in the Interlocken business park makes up a meaningful share of Broomfield exchange volume. Grocery-anchored and lifestyle retail near Flatiron Marketplace draws steady interest. Flex and light industrial space is present but limited, tucked mostly along the edges of the business park. A handful of newer multifamily projects near the retail node have also traded as investors look to diversify away from the office-heavy reputation the city has carried for years, and that shift has only picked up as more remote-work-era tenants reassess their office footprint. Categories worth tracking:

  • Corporate office in and around the Interlocken business park
  • Grocery-anchored and lifestyle retail near Flatiron Marketplace
  • Flex and light industrial space on the business park's edges
  • Multifamily serving the corporate workforce
  • DST interests for owners exiting single-tenant office risk

sections.heading: Forward Exchange Is the Default Play
sections.html: Most Broomfield sellers run a standard forward exchange, selling the relinquished property first and identifying replacements within 45 days. Single-tenant office carries more tenant concentration risk than the retail side, so a seller exiting a single-tenant building should build a longer identification list in case that one tenant's lease status changes mid-process. A tenant renewal notice that arrives during the identification window has changed more than one seller's plan here, and it's exactly the kind of surprise a longer candidate list is meant to absorb.

sections.heading: Boot Shows Up More Often Than Sellers Expect
sections.html: Because Interlocken office trades at a high price point, sellers moving into a smaller or lower-value replacement can end up with taxable boot they didn't plan for. I walk every Broomfield seller through the math before they fall for a property that's meaningfully smaller than what they're selling, so there are no surprises at closing. Debt relief is part of that math too, alongside any cash received, and sellers sometimes overlook it.

sections.heading: Coordinating a Corporate-Scale Deal
sections.html: Financing on Interlocken-scale office moves slower than a retail purchase, and lenders want a clear look at tenant credit before committing. The qualified intermediary, lender, and the investor's CPA all need to be looped in early, especially when boot is a real possibility, so nobody is doing that math for the first time at the closing table. I schedule a boot review call with the CPA before the identification list is finalized on every deal like this, and I've seen that single call change which properties actually make the final list.

faqs.q: Why does Broomfield office trade differently than office in Denver?
faqs.a: The Interlocken corridor along US-36 has drawn large corporate and tech tenants on longer leases, which produces steadier income but more concentration risk in single-tenant buildings than the more varied office stock closer to downtown Denver. That risk profile changes how buyers underwrite the asset and how a lender views the loan, sometimes requiring a larger down payment to offset the concentration, particularly on a building with only one or two tenants, since the loan is really a bet on that tenant's staying power.

faqs.q: What is boot, and why does it come up in Broomfield exchanges?
faqs.a: Boot is any value received in the exchange that isn't like-kind real property, including cash or debt relief, and it becomes taxable. Because Interlocken office trades at a high price point, sellers moving into a smaller replacement should check the math before assuming a full deferral, since debt relief alone can create boot even without cash changing hands.

faqs.q: Is single-tenant office a risky 1031 replacement in Broomfield?
faqs.a: It carries more tenant concentration risk than a multi-tenant building or retail asset, since income depends on one lease. A longer identification list gives an investor room to pivot if that tenant's situation changes during the exchange, which happens more often here than sellers expect.

faqs.q: How fast does financing move on Interlocken-scale office purchases?
faqs.a: Slower than a typical retail deal. Lenders want a full look at tenant credit and lease terms, so involve a lender well before the 45-day identification deadline rather than after, especially if the tenant roster includes more than one company.

faqs.q: Can 1031 Exchange Denver calculate my boot exposure on a Broomfield deal?
faqs.a: No. This service coordinates identification and scheduling among the investor's advisors. Boot calculations and tax exposure are determined by the investor's CPA or tax attorney based on the specific transaction numbers, and that review should happen before the identification list is finalized.
